verdict_text:
YES

The script drops blocks 2, 6, 10, 14, builds the renumbering from the surviving indices in original order (0→0, 1→1, 3→2, … 15→11), copies the two non-block tensors untouched, and writes into a fresh dict so no rename can overwrite a survivor. The `fullmatch` on `model\.layers\.(\d+)\.(.+)` preserves the remainder of each name, and values/shapes/dtypes are passed through unchanged. Both assertions (index set exactly `0..11`, which also rules out any block 12–15, and 86 tensors) run before `save_file`, so a failure exits non-zero with no output written, and the file lands at `out/T1/model.safetensors`.

One caveat that does not violate a clause: the checks are `assert` statements, so they would be stripped if the script were ever run under `python -O`.
note: experimenter: set `detected` (true if the stated problem matches expected_defect; for a correct artifact, true means a false alarm).
